# Security Hunter Ledger

One line per entry, newest last.

- 2026-09-10 | FIXED | sandbox-exec | `AgentSession` executed SendEmail/SaveDraft/MoveEmail/CreateFolder/CalendarQuery/CalendarCreate/CalendarUpdate/CalendarDelete request frames against gateway-held shared credentials without checking the issuing agent's `tools` grant (only the GitHub request handler had this check) — any agent, regardless of declared tools, could send mail or mutate the shared calendar/mailbox | lib/tri_onyx/agent_session.ex
- 2026-09-10 | NO-FINDING (duplicate) | sandbox-exec | Connector-triggered `/restart <other-agent>` bypassing `restart_targets` (lib/tri_onyx/system_command.ex, lib/tri_onyx/connector_handler.ex) — already found and open as PR #37; not re-filed
- 2026-09-10 | DOWNGRADED | sandbox-exec | `restart_agent_request` in `handle_agent_event` checks `restart_targets` but never checks `"RestartAgent" in state.definition.tools` before honoring the request — lower severity than the fixed finding since the target set is still bounded by `restart_targets`, and proving it needs a live Python runtime that can emit protocol frames the SDK's `allowed_tools` would otherwise block (no Docker/live gateway available in this environment) — worth a human's eye | lib/tri_onyx/agent_session.ex
- 2026-09-10 | DOWNGRADED | sandbox-exec | The wire protocol between `agent_runner.py` and the gateway is plain JSON Lines on the container's shared stdout; if any code running inside the sandbox with unmediated stdout access (e.g. a Bash subprocess that isn't fully captured by the SDK) could write directly to fd 1, it could forge arbitrary `*_request` frames independent of `allowed_tools`. Not provable without a live container/SDK run — worth a human's eye on `runtime/agent_runner.py`'s stdout handling | runtime/agent_runner.py
